h: Steam Trains and a Queen's Resting Place
p: Peterborough has a couple of family favourites that pair nicely with a session at Flip Out. The Nene Valley Railway runs heritage steam and diesel trains between Wansford and Peterborough, passing Ferry Meadows on the way. Riding a steam train is a real treat for kids, and there are special events throughout the year.

Peterborough Cathedral is famous for its stunning west front, but it's also the resting place of Catherine of Aragon, Henry VIII's first wife. Visitors often leave pomegranates at her grave, her personal symbol.
Peterborough Museum, on Priestgate, is a good spot for a rainy day, with local history and an old operating theatre from when the building was a hospital.

In the city centre, Cathedral Square is a lovely open space surrounded by historic buildings, including the Guildhall, which sits on pillars. It's a nice spot to grab a coffee and soak up the atmosphere.

A short drive north, Burghley House, near Stamford, is a grand Elizabethan house with a deer park and gardens. Further south, Hamerton Zoo Park, near Sawtry, is a family-friendly zoo with a big range of animals.
Peterborough United play at London Road, so check the fixtures if you're driving through on a Saturday.
Families who love the outdoors can also follow the Green Wheel, a network of cycle paths and walking routes that circles the city.
With good road and rail links, Peterborough is easy to reach and makes a great base for a family weekend in Cambridgeshire.
